claims.statement: Adjunctive pramipexole improved the primary continuous SHAPS score versus placebo at nine weeks in the modified ITT anhedonic-depression population. Dichotomized response and remission comparisons were not significant; they use a different scoring system.

Nominal week 9 DARS and AES-S differences favored pramipexole, whereas MADRS-S, HDRS-6, GAD-7, ISI and BBQ endpoint comparisons were not significant. Secondary tests were unadjusted for multiplicity; nonsignificance is not equivalence.

The nine-week randomized period reported no serious adverse events but frequent adverse symptoms, modified impulse-control assessments and two active-arm patients with mild manic symptoms. The selected extension reported three serious events in two patients, judged unrelated by investigators. These observations do not establish general safety.

A nested exploratory fMRI sample showed relative preservation of ventral striatal reward-anticipation BOLD versus a decrease on placebo. The active-arm SHAPS/BOLD correlation had P .060; this does not establish D3 occupancy or causal mediation.

Exploratory LPA and waking-time analyses showed overall treatment effects in a valid-data subset, but LPA was not significantly different at week 9, sedentary time did not consistently decrease and MVPA did not consistently increase. Movement is not proof of clinical benefit.

Selected open-label completers had descriptive symptom improvements, with all patients receiving pramipexole and substantial attrition. Former randomized arm labels do not provide a six-month placebo comparison or independent replication.
